text: If it had not rained on a certain May morning Valancy Stirling’s whole life would have been entirely different.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: She would have gone, with the rest of her clan, to Aunt Wellington’s engagement picnic and Dr. Trent would have gone to Montreal.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: But it did rain and you shall hear what happened to her because of it.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy wakened early, in the lifeless, hopeless hour just preceding dawn.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: She had not slept very well.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: One does not sleep well, sometimes, when one is twenty-nine on the morrow, and unmarried, in a community and connection where the unmarried are simply those who have failed to get a man.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Deerwood and the Stirlings had long since relegated Valancy to hopeless old maidenhood.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: But Valancy herself had never quite relinquished a certain pitiful, shamed, little hope that Romance would come her way yet⁠—never, until this wet, horrible morning, when she wakened to the fact that she was twenty-nine and unsought by any man.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Ay, there lay the sting.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy did not mind so much being an old maid.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: After all, she thought, being an old maid couldn’t possibly be as dreadful as being married to an Uncle Wellington or an Uncle Benjamin, or even an Uncle Herbert.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: What hurt her was that she had never had a chance to be anything but an old maid.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: No man had ever desired her.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: The tears came into her eyes as she lay there alone in the faintly greying darkness.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: She dared not let herself cry as hard as she wanted to, for two reasons.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: She was afraid that crying might bring on another attack of that pain around the heart.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: She had had a spell of it after she had got into bed⁠—rather worse than any she had had yet.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: And she was afraid her mother would notice her red eyes at breakfast and keep at her with minute, persistent, mosquito-like questions regarding the cause thereof.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: “Suppose,” thought Valancy with a ghastly grin, “I answered with the plain truth, ‘I am crying because I cannot get married.’
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: How horrified Mother would be⁠—though she is ashamed every day of her life of her old maid daughter.”
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: But of course appearances should be kept up.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: “It is not,” Valancy could hear her mother’s prim, dictatorial voice asserting, “it is not maidenly to think about men.”
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: The thought of her mother’s expression made Valancy laugh⁠—for she had a sense of humour nobody in her clan suspected.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: For that matter, there were a good many things about Valancy that nobody suspected.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: But her laughter was very superficial and presently she lay there, a huddled, futile little figure, listening to the rain pouring down outside and watching, with a sick distaste, the chill, merciless light creeping into her ugly, sordid room.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: She knew the ugliness of that room by heart⁠—knew it and hated it.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: The yellow-painted floor, with one hideous, “hooked” rug by the bed, with a grotesque, “hooked” dog on it, always grinning at her when she awoke; the faded, dark-red paper; the ceiling discoloured by old leaks and crossed by cracks; the narrow, pinched little washstand; the brown-paper lambrequin with purple roses on it; the spotted old looking-glass with the crack across it, propped up on the inadequate dressing-table; the jar of ancient potpourri made by her mother in her mythical honeymoon; the shell-covered box, with one burst corner, which Cousin Stickles had made in her equally mythical girlhood; the beaded pincushion with half its bead fringe gone; the one stiff, yellow chair; the faded old motto, “Gone but not forgotten,” worked in coloured yarns about Great-grandmother Stirling’s grim old face; the old photographs of ancient relatives long banished from the rooms below.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: There were only two pictures that were not of relatives.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: One, an old chromo of a puppy sitting on a rainy doorstep.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: That picture always made Valancy unhappy.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: That forlorn little dog crouched on the doorstep in the driving rain!
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Why didn’t someone open the door and let him in?
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: The other picture was a faded, passe-partouted engraving of Queen Louise coming down a stairway, which Aunt Wellington had lavishly given her on her tenth birthday.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: For nineteen years she had looked at it and hated it, beautiful, smug, self-satisfied Queen Louise.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: But she never dared destroy it or remove it.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Mother and Cousin Stickles would have been aghast, or, as Valancy irreverently expressed it in her thoughts, would have had a fit.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Every room in the house was ugly, of course.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: But downstairs appearances were kept up somewhat.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: There was no money for rooms nobody ever saw.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy sometimes felt that she could have done something for her room herself, even without money, if she were permitted.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: But her mother had negatived every timid suggestion and Valancy did not persist.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy never persisted.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: She was afraid to.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Her mother could not brook opposition.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Mrs. Stirling would sulk for days if offended, with the airs of an insulted duchess.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: The only thing Valancy liked about her room was that she could be alone there at night to cry if she wanted to.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: But, after all, what did it matter if a room, which you used for nothing except sleeping and dressing in, were ugly?
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy was never permitted to stay alone in her room for any other purpose.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: People who wanted to be alone, so Mrs. Frederick Stirling and Cousin Stickles believed, could only want to be alone for some sinister purpose.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: But her room in the Blue Castle was everything a room should be.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy, so cowed and subdued and overridden and snubbed in real life, was wont to let herself go rather splendidly in her daydreams.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Nobody in the Stirling clan, or its ramifications, suspected this, least of all her mother and Cousin Stickles.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: They never knew that Valancy had two homes⁠—the ugly red brick box of a home, on Elm Street, and the Blue Castle in Spain.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy had lived spiritually in the Blue Castle ever since she could remember.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: She had been a very tiny child when she found herself possessed of it.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Always, when she shut her eyes, she could see it plainly, with its turrets and banners on the pine-clad mountain height, wrapped in its faint, blue loveliness, against the sunset skies of a fair and unknown land.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Everything wonderful and beautiful was in that castle.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Jewels that queens might have worn; robes of moonlight and fire; couches of roses and gold; long flights of shallow marble steps, with great, white urns, and with slender, mist-clad maidens going up and down them; courts, marble-pillared, where shimmering fountains fell and nightingales sang among the myrtles; halls of mirrors that reflected only handsome knights and lovely women⁠—herself the loveliest of all, for whose glance men died.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: All that supported her through the boredom of her days was the hope of going on a dream spree at night.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Most, if not all, of the Stirlings would have died of horror if they had known half the things Valancy did in her Blue Castle.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: For one thing she had quite a few lovers in it.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Oh, only one at a time.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: One who wooed her with all the romantic ardour of the age of chivalry and won her after long devotion and many deeds of derring-do, and was wedded to her with pomp and circumstance in the great, banner-hung chapel of the Blue Castle.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: At twelve, this lover was a fair lad with golden curls and heavenly blue eyes.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: At fifteen, he was tall and dark and pale, but still necessarily handsome.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: At twenty, he was ascetic, dreamy, spiritual.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: At twenty-five, he had a clean-cut jaw, slightly grim, and a face strong and rugged rather than handsome.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy never grew older than twenty-five in her Blue Castle, but recently⁠—very recently⁠—her hero had had reddish, tawny hair, a twisted smile and a mysterious past.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: I don’t say Valancy deliberately murdered these lovers as she outgrew them.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: One simply faded away as another came.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Things are very convenient in this respect in Blue Castles.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: But, on this morning of her day of fate, Valancy could not find the key of her Blue Castle.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Reality pressed on her too hardly, barking at her heels like a maddening little dog.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: She was twenty-nine, lonely, undesired, ill-favoured⁠—the only homely girl in a handsome clan, with no past and no future.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: As far as she could look back, life was drab and colourless, with not one single crimson or purple spot anywhere.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: As far as she could look forward it seemed certain to be just the same until she was nothing but a solitary, little withered leaf clinging to a wintry bough.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: The moment when a woman realises that she has nothing to live for⁠—neither love, duty, purpose nor hope⁠—holds for her the bitterness of death.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: “And I just have to go on living because I can’t stop.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: I may have to live eighty years,” thought Valancy, in a kind of panic.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: “We’re all horribly long-lived.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: It sickens me to think of it.”
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: She was glad it was raining⁠—or rather, she was drearily satisfied that it was raining.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: There would be no picnic that day.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: This annual picnic, whereby Aunt and Uncle Wellington⁠—one always thought of them in that succession⁠—inevitably celebrated their engagement at a picnic thirty years before, had been, of late years, a veritable nightmare to Valancy.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: By an impish coincidence it was the same day as her birthday and, after she had passed twenty-five, nobody let her forget it.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Much as she hated going to the picnic, it would never have occurred to her to rebel against it.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: There seemed to be nothing of the revolutionary in her nature.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: And she knew exactly what everyone would say to her at the picnic.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Uncle Wellington, whom she disliked and despised even though he had fulfilled the highest Stirling aspiration, “marrying money,” would say to her in a pig’s whisper, “Not thinking of getting married yet, my dear?” and then go off into the bellow of laughter with which he invariably concluded his dull remarks.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Aunt Wellington, of whom Valancy stood in abject awe, would tell her about Olive’s new chiffon dress and Cecil’s last devoted letter.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy would have to look as pleased and interested as if the dress and letter had been hers or else Aunt Wellington would be offended.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: And Valancy had long ago decided that she would rather offend God than Aunt Wellington, because God might forgive her but Aunt Wellington never would.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Aunt Alberta, enormously fat, with an amiable habit of always referring to her husband as “he,” as if he were the only male creature in the world, who could never forget that she had been a great beauty in her youth, would condole with Valancy on her sallow skin⁠—
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: “I don’t know why all the girls of today are so sunburned.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: When I was a girl my skin was roses and cream.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: I was counted the prettiest girl in Canada, my dear.”
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Perhaps Uncle Herbert wouldn’t say anything⁠—or perhaps he would remark jocularly, “How fat you’re getting, Doss!”
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: And then everybody would laugh over the excessively humorous idea of poor, scrawny little Doss getting fat.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Handsome, solemn Uncle James, whom Valancy disliked but respected because he was reputed to be very clever and was therefore the clan oracle⁠—brains being none too plentiful in the Stirling connection⁠—would probably remark with the owl-like sarcasm that had won him his reputation, “I suppose you’re busy with your hope-chest these days?”
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: And Uncle Benjamin would ask some of his abominable conundrums, between wheezy chuckles, and answer them himself.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: “What is the difference between Doss and a mouse?
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: “The mouse wishes to harm the cheese and Doss wishes to charm the he’s.”
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy had heard him ask that riddle fifty times and every time she wanted to throw something at him.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: But she never did.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: In the first place, the Stirlings simply did not throw things; in the second place, Uncle Benjamin was a wealthy and childless old widower and Valancy had been brought up in the fear and admonition of his money.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: If she offended him he would cut her out of his will⁠—supposing she were in it.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy did not want to be cut out of Uncle Benjamin’s will.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: She had been poor all her life and knew the galling bitterness of it.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: So she endured his riddles and even smiled tortured little smiles over them.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Aunt Isabel, downright and disagreeable as an east wind, would criticise her in some way⁠—Valancy could not predict just how, for Aunt Isabel never repeated a criticism⁠—she found something new with which to jab you every time.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Aunt Isabel prided herself on saying what she thought, but didn’t like it so well when other people said what they thought to her.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy never said what she thought.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Cousin Georgiana⁠—named after her great-great-grandmother, who had been named after George the Fourth⁠—would recount dolorously the names of all relatives and friends who had died since the last picnic and wonder “which of us will be the first to go next.”
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Oppressively competent, Aunt Mildred would talk endlessly of her husband and her odious prodigies of babies to Valancy, because Valancy would be the only one she could find to put up with it.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: For the same reason, Cousin Gladys⁠—really First Cousin Gladys once removed, according to the strict way in which the Stirlings tabulated relationship⁠—a tall, thin lady who admitted she had a sensitive disposition, would describe minutely the tortures of her neuritis.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: And Olive, the wonder girl of the whole Stirling clan, who had everything Valancy had not⁠—beauty, popularity, love⁠—would show off her beauty and presume on her popularity and flaunt her diamond insignia of love in Valancy’s dazzled, envious eyes.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: There would be none of all this today.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: And there would be no packing up of teaspoons.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: The packing up was always left for Valancy and Cousin Stickles.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: And once, six years ago, a silver teaspoon from Aunt Wellington’s wedding set had been lost.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy never heard the last of that silver teaspoon.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Its ghost appeared Banquo-like at every subsequent family feast.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Oh, yes, Valancy knew exactly what the picnic would be like and she blessed the rain that had saved her from it.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: There would be no picnic this year.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: If Aunt Wellington could not celebrate on the sacred day itself she would have no celebration at all.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Thank whatever gods there were for that.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Since there would be no picnic, Valancy made up her mind that, if the rain held up in the afternoon, she would go up to the library and get another of John Foster’s books.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy was never allowed to read novels, but John Foster’s books were not novels.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: They were “nature books”⁠—so the librarian told Mrs. Frederick Stirling⁠—“all about the woods and birds and bugs and things like that, you know.”
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: So Valancy was allowed to read them⁠—under protest, for it was only too evident that she enjoyed them too much.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: It was permissible, even laudable, to read to improve your mind and your religion, but a book that was enjoyable was dangerous.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy did not know whether her mind was being improved or not; but she felt vaguely that if she had come across John Foster’s books years ago life might have been a different thing for her.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: They seemed to her to yield glimpses of a world into which she might once have entered, though the door was forever barred to her now.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: It was only within the last year that John Foster’s books had been in the Deerwood library, though the librarian told Valancy that he had been a well-known writer for several years.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: “Where does he live?”
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy had asked.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: “Nobody knows.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: From his books he must be a Canadian, but no more information can be had.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: His publishers won’t say a word.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Quite likely John Foster is a nom de plume.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: His books are so popular we can’t keep them in at all, though I really can’t see what people find in them to rave over.”
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: “I think they’re wonderful,” said Valancy, timidly.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: “Oh⁠—well⁠—” Miss Clarkson smiled in a patronising fashion that relegated Valancy’s opinions to limbo, “I can’t say I care much for bugs myself.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: But certainly Foster seems to know all there is to know about them.”
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy didn’t know whether she cared much for bugs either.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: It was not John Foster’s uncanny knowledge of wild creatures and insect life that enthralled her.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: She could hardly say what it was⁠—some tantalising lure of a mystery never revealed⁠—some hint of a great secret just a little further on⁠—some faint, elusive echo of lovely, forgotten things⁠—John Foster’s magic was indefinable.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Yes, she would get a new Foster book.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: It was a month since she had Thistle Harvest, so surely Mother could not object.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Valancy had read it four times⁠—she knew whole passages off by heart.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Mrs. Ferrars died on the night of the 16th⁠–⁠17th September⁠—a Thursday.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: I was sent for at eight o’clock on the morning of Friday the 17th.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: There was nothing to be done.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: She had been dead some hours.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: It was just a few minutes after nine when I reached home once more.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: I opened the front door with my latchkey, and purposely delayed a few moments in the hall, hanging up my hat and the light overcoat that I had deemed a wise precaution against the chill of an early autumn morning.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: To tell the truth, I was considerably upset and worried.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: I am not going to pretend that at that moment I foresaw the events of the next few weeks.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: I emphatically did not do so.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: But my instinct told me that there were stirring times ahead.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: From the dining room on my left there came the rattle of teacups and the short, dry cough of my sister Caroline.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: “Is that you, James?” she called.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: An unnecessary question, since who else could it be?
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: To tell the truth, it was precisely my sister Caroline who was the cause of my few minutes’ delay.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: The motto of the mongoose family, so Mr. Kipling tells us, is: “Go and find out.”
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: If Caroline ever adopts a crest, I should certainly suggest a mongoose rampant.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: One might omit the first part of the motto.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Caroline can do any amount of finding out by sitting placidly at home.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: I don’t know how she manages it, but there it is.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: I suspect that the servants and the tradesmen constitute her Intelligence Corps.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: When she goes out, it is not to gather in information, but to spread it.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: At that, too, she is amazingly expert.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: It was really this last named trait of hers which was causing me these pangs of indecision.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Whatever I told Caroline now concerning the demise of Mrs. Ferrars would be common knowledge all over the village within the space of an hour and a half.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: As a professional man, I naturally aim at discretion.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Therefore I have got into the habit of continually withholding all information possible from my sister.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: She usually finds out just the same, but I have the moral satisfaction of knowing that I am in no way to blame.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Mrs. Ferrars’ husband died just over a year ago, and Caroline has constantly asserted, without the least foundation for the assertion, that his wife poisoned him.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: She scorns my invariable rejoinder that Mr. Ferrars died of acute gastritis, helped on by habitual overindulgence in alcoholic beverages.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: The symptoms of gastritis and arsenical poisoning are not, I agree, unlike, but Caroline bases her accusation on quite different lines.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: “You’ve only got to look at her,” I have heard her say.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated

text: Mrs. Ferrars, though not in her first youth, was a very attractive woman, and her clothes, though simple, always seemed to fit her very well, but all the same, lots of women buy their clothes in Paris, and have not, on that account, necessarily poisoned their husbands.
labeler: Codex and independent Claude labeler; coordinator adjudicated
